title: Lightweight Machine Learning for Classifying Disaster-Related Social Media Posts
summary: The paper asks whether lightweight TF-IDF classifiers can handle short, semantically overlapping, and strongly imbalanced disaster-related social-media posts in CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian classification. It compares TF-IDF representations and linear/naive Bayes classifiers on predefined Train/Development splits, locks a balanced LinearSVC with unigram–bigram TF-IDF and C=0.5, refits on Train+Development, and evaluates once on Test, adding per-label, margin, resource and tropical-cyclone analyses. The locked model reaches Accuracy 0.8282, Macro-F1 0.6578 and Weighted-F1 0.8315 on Test, with lower decision margins associated with errors and a small in-domain benefit but much lower resource use for a cyclone specialist.

why: No author repository or code link is provided, so there is no released implementation to run or repair. The experiment is nonetheless a small classical NLP pipeline (TF-IDF plus LinearSVC) that can be reimplemented directly from the paper and claim contract on this CPU-only machine.
est_runtime: About 10-20 minutes of command time, dominated by obtaining/preparing CrisisBench and fitting a few sparse TF-IDF plus LinearSVC models; the reported vectorization and fitting times are only a few seconds per model.
blockers: No author code was released or linked.
The dataset acquisition path is underspecified in the paper; CrisisBench v1.0 must be located manually.
No GPU is available, but this is not a blocker for sparse TF-IDF and LinearSVC.

approach: We reimplement the paper's locked pipeline from scratch with scikit-learn: acquire the official CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian consolidated files with their predefined splits, verify the exact 61,164/8,935/17,356 record counts, apply the paper's conservative normalisation to text_clean only, and build word unigram–bigram TF-IDF with min_df=2, max_df=0.95, sublinear term frequency, L2 normalisation and float32 output. We first reproduce the Development-stage checkpoint with a vectorizer fit on Train only (targeting Accuracy 0.8245 and Macro-F1 0.6413), then refit a fresh vectorizer and LinearSVC(C=0.5, class_weight='balanced') on Train+Development (70,099 records) and evaluate exactly once on Test to obtain C1–C3, together with per-label metrics, decision margins and timings. We then rebuild the broad tropical-cyclone subset from the event field (17,586 train+dev and 4,358 test records), train the specialist with identical settings, and score the general locked model on the same subset to obtain C6/C7, while reporting TF-IDF feature counts for C8. Because the paper gives no dataset URL, the acquisition script tries Hugging Face, the QCRI CrisisBench site and GitHub mirrors, and hard-gates on the published record counts; if no candidate matches it writes a blocked status instead of fabricating numbers.
steps: Create directories (data/raw, data/processed, results, logs) and install pinned-ish dependencies: pip install --quiet numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm datasets huggingface_hub gdown; log pip freeze and Python/sklearn versions to logs/env.txt.

Run src/acquire.py: search Hugging Face Hub for datasets matching 'crisisbench' and try likely configs (humanitarian/english/default); if that fails, scrape https://crisisnlp.qcri.org/crisisbench and https://crisisnlp.qcri.org for .zip/.tar.gz/.csv links and download with requests (gdown for Google Drive links); if that fails, use the GitHub API to search for CrisisBench repositories, shallow-clone candidates into data/raw and scan for tabular files with a text column. Unzip with Python zipfile/tarfile only.

Validate acquisition: require 61,164 Train, 8,935 Development, 17,356 Test records, 87,455 total and exactly 11 labels; record source URL, sha256, file names and detected columns in data/manifest.json. If no candidate satisfies all checks, write results/metrics.json with status='blocked' and the observed counts, then exit non-zero instead of continuing.

Map columns in src/data.py: prefer an existing text_clean column, else use text and generate text_clean; resolve label column among label_humanitarian/label/class and event column among event/event_name; normalise label strings by stripping whitespace and assert the union has exactly 11 labels. Drop/forbid event, source, id, lang and lang_conf from any feature matrix.

Apply src/preprocess.py to every row: strip leading RT marker, replace URLs with 'url', @mentions with 'user', delete '#' characters only, lowercase, collapse whitespace. Assert no NaN and less than 1% empty strings, and log 20 before/after examples for eyeball validation.

Run the Development-stage checkpoint in src/experiments.py: fit a fresh TfidfVectorizer on Train only, transform Development, fit LinearSVC(C=0.5, class_weight='balanced', random_state=42), and compute Accuracy, Macro-F1 over all 11 labels and Weighted-F1 plus per-label metrics. Compare against C5=0.8245 and C4=0.6413 with the 0.01 band; write results/dev_metrics.json and a diagnostic note if the checkpoint misses.

Request the full smoke run (python reproduce.py --smoke) on a stratified 3,000/1,000/1,000 subsample; confirm the JSON schema, non-NaN metrics, finite margins and plausible dummy-baseline comparison before spending time on the full run.

Locked final fit: concatenate Train+Development (assert 70,099 rows), fit a fresh TfidfVectorizer with the locked settings, assert the vocabulary size is about 110,414 (within 2% relative), fit a fresh LinearSVC with C=0.5 and class_weight='balanced', and time vectorisation and fitting separately with perf_counter.

Transform Test once, predict once, and compute Accuracy, Macro-F1 (all 11 labels), Weighted-F1, per-label Precision/Recall/F1, the 11×11 confusion matrix and the decision margin (top1 minus top2 of decision_function) overall, by correctness and per label. Save predictions, margins and true labels to results/test_predictions.csv.gz and the metrics to results/test_metrics.json.

Build the broad tropical-cyclone subset with a case-insensitive regex on the event field (typhoon|hurricane|cyclone) and assert 17,586 train+dev records and 4,358 test records (21,944 total). If counts differ by more than 1%, log the observed counts and mark C6/C7 as unverified rather than silently adjusting the filter.

Train the cyclone specialist with identical locked settings but only on broad cyclone train+dev records; assert its feature count is about 30,168 (within 2% relative); evaluate on the broad cyclone Test subset to obtain C6. Filter the general model's Test predictions to the same 4,358 records to obtain C7, and report margins and timings for both models.

Assemble results/metrics.json in src/report.py: for each claim C1–C8 record paper value, achieved value, absolute delta, tolerance, pass boolean and the exact configuration used; include the dataset manifest, split counts, label list with counts, per-label metrics, margin statistics, timings, feature counts, dev checkpoint, dummy baseline and an overall status field.

Run the full pipeline end-to-end with python reproduce.py --full, then re-run once from a clean results/ directory to confirm determinism of the deterministic estimator path; verify results/metrics.json parses and that the entrypoint prints the final Test Macro-F1 next to 0.6578.

Write a short results/README.md summarising which requirement drove each artefact, which assumption ids were exercised (A1, A3, A4, A6, A7, A9, A11, A12) and any residual mismatch, especially if the dataset source differs from the paper's unspecified release.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: stratified subsample of 3,000 Train / 1,000 Development / 1,000 Test (falling back to all rows if a split is smaller), run acquire-validate, preprocess, the dev-stage fit, the locked-style refit on the subsampled Train+Development, one Test evaluation, the cyclone filter (using the subsample), and report. Assert: the JSON parses; keys C1–C8, per-label metrics, margins and timings exist; Accuracy/Macro-F1/Weighted-F1 are finite and in [0,1]; vocabulary size and coefficient shape (n_labels, n_features) are consistent; a stratified smoke run on real data completes in under two minutes.
intermediate_checks: Split sizes are exactly 61,164 / 8,935 / 17,356 (total 87,455) and Train+Development is exactly 70,099; mismatch halts the run with a blocked status and observed counts.
Exactly 11 unique labels after stripping whitespace; every Test label appears in the Train+Development label union; per-split label counts and imbalance ratio (largest/smallest class) are logged.
text_clean has no NaN and less than 1% empty strings; mean and 95th-percentile token counts are in a plausible short-text range (roughly 5–40 tokens) and 20 before/after examples are logged.
Feature leakage guard: assert the vectorizer is fitted on a matrix built only from text_clean and that event/source/id/lang/lang_conf are absent from the DataFrame passed to it.

Development checkpoint gate: Accuracy within ±0.01 of 0.8245 and Macro-F1 within ±0.01 of 0.6413 before trusting the Test numbers; if it misses, log label mapping, duplicate rows and preprocessing differences.

Dummy baseline: most-frequent-class Development Accuracy and Macro-F1 (expected Accuracy around 0.3–0.5 and near-zero Macro-F1), confirming the task is genuinely imbalanced and that the real model beats it substantially.
General vectorizer on Train+Development yields about 110,414 features (within 2% relative) and a (11, n_features) coefficient matrix; the specialist yields about 30,168 features.
No unresolved sklearn ConvergenceWarning: if LinearSVC warns at max_iter=1000, refit once with max_iter=20000, record max_iter_used and confirm coefficients are finite.
Decision margins are finite, positive by construction, and the mean margin for correct Test predictions exceeds the mean margin for incorrect ones.
Timing sanity: vectorisation and fitting for the general model each complete in seconds (paper reports about 2.2 s and 1.9 s), so a run taking many minutes signals a data or configuration problem.
budget_plan: About 2 minutes environment setup and dependency installation; up to 8 minutes for data acquisition and validation, which is the dominant risk and may involve trying several mirrors and unzipping; about 2 minutes for the smoke run; about 3 minutes for the Development checkpoint, the locked Train+Development fit, the single Test evaluation and the tropical-cyclone specialist and subset analysis (each sparse TF-IDF plus LinearSVC fit is seconds on CPU); about 1 minute to assemble results/metrics.json and re-verify determinism. Roughly 2 minutes are held back for retrying an alternate data mirror, giving a 15–20 minute total that fits the estimated 10–20 minute reference runtime; if acquisition fails at every source, the budget ends early with an explicit blocked report.

﻿Description of the dataset
==========================
The Crisis Benchmarks Dataset consists of data from different data sources [1]):


Data format and directories
===========================
The data directory contains the following sub-directories. In each directory, there are files for Informativeness and Humanitarian tasks.

* data/all_data_en -- all combined english dataset used for the experiments
* data/individual_data_en -- consists of data used for the experiments as individual data source such as crisisnlp and crisislex
* data/event_aware_en -- all combined english dataset with event tag (fire, earthquake, flood, ...) are tagged
* data/data_split_all_lang -- all combined dataset with their train/dev and test splits
* data/initial_filtering -- all combined dataset duplicate removed data
* data/class_label_mapped -- all combined dataset initial set of dataset where class label mapped

Format of the TSV files
---------------------------------------------------------
Each TSV file contains the following columns, separated by a tab:
* id: corresponds to the user tweet id from Twitter.
* event: event name associated with the respective dataset
* source: source of the dataset
* text: tweet text.
* lang: language tag obtained either from Twitter or obtained from Google language detection API
* lang conf: confidence score obtained from Google language detection API; for many cases, there are tag "NA", which represents that the language tag is obtained from Twitter from Google API
* class_label: class label a given tweet text.

import os, re, html, time, json
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.svm import LinearSVC
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score

P = os.path.join(os.environ['REPRO_DATA_CACHE'], 'crisisbench_official', 'en')
SPL = {}


def load():
    for s in ['train', 'dev', 'test']:
        SPL[s] = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(P, 'crisis_consolidated_humanitarian_filtered_lang_en_%s.tsv' % s),
                             sep='\t', dtype=str, quoting=3, keep_default_na=False)


def clean(t, do_unescape=True, do_rt=True):
    if do_unescape:
        t = html.unescape(t)
    if do_rt:
        t = re.sub(r'^\s*RT\b[:\s]*', ' ', t, flags=re.I)
    t = re.sub(r'https?://\S+|www\.\S+', ' url ', t, flags=re.I)
    t = re.sub(r'@\w+', ' user ', t)
    t = t.replace('#', '')
    t = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', t).strip().lower()
    return t


def run(tag, **kw):
    tr = SPL['train']['text'].map(lambda x: clean(x, **kw))
    dv = SPL['dev']['text'].map(lambda x: clean(x, **kw))
    ytr = SPL['train']['class_label'].values
    ydv = SPL['dev']['class_label'].values
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    vec = TfidfVectorizer(ngram_range=(1, 2), min_df=2, max_df=0.95, sublinear_tf=True,
                          norm='l2', dtype=np.float32, lowercase=True, stop_words=None)
    Xtr = vec.fit_transform(tr)
    Xdv = vec.transform(dv)
    t1 = time.perf_counter()
    clf = LinearSVC(C=0.5, class_weight='balanced', random_state=42)
    clf.fit(Xtr, ytr)
    t2 = time.perf_counter()
    pred = clf.predict(Xdv)
    acc = accuracy_score(ydv, pred)
    mf1 = f1_score(ydv, pred, average='macro', zero_division=0)
    wf1 = f1_score(ydv, pred, average='weighted', zero_division=0)
    print(f'{tag}: feats={len(vec.vocabulary_)} acc={acc:.4f} macroF1={mf1:.4f} wF1={wf1:.4f} '
          f'vec={t1-t0:.2f}s fit={t2-t1:.2f}s')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    load()
    print({s: len(d) for s, d in SPL.items()})
    run('A_full_clean')
    run('B_no_unescape', do_unescape=False)
    run('C_no_rt', do_rt=False)

"""Deterministic, conservative text preprocessing (R2, R3, R4, A5, A6).

Pipeline applied to every split's raw `text` field to produce `text_clean`:
  HTML entity decode -> drop a leading RT marker -> URLs -> 'url' -> @mentions -> 'user'
  -> delete '#' characters only (hashtag text retained) -> collapse whitespace -> lowercase.

No stop-word filtering, stemming, lemmatisation or custom tokenisation (R4).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import re

from . import config

_RT = re.compile(config.RT_RE, re.IGNORECASE)
_URL = re.compile(config.URL_RE, re.IGNORECASE)
_MENTION = re.compile(config.MENTION_RE)
_WS = re.compile(r"\s+")


def clean_text(text: str) -> str:
    if text is None:
        return ""
    t = str(text)
    if config.HTML_UNESCAPE:
        t = html.unescape(t)
    t = _RT.sub(" ", t)
    t = _URL.sub(" url ", t)
    t = _MENTION.sub(" user ", t)
    t = t.replace("#", "")
    t = _WS.sub(" ", t).strip()
    if config.LOWERCASE:
        t = t.lower()
    return t


def clean_series(series):
    return series.astype(str).map(clean_text)


def audit_examples(series, n=20):
    """Before/after examples for eyeball validation."""
    out = []
    for raw in series.head(n):
        out.append({"raw": str(raw)[:300], "clean": clean_text(raw)[:300]})
    return out

The paper gives no URL or checksum, so we fetch the official QCRI release for the
predefined Train / Development / Test splits.  Two independent sources are tried:

  1. Hugging Face mirror ``QCRI/CrisisBench-english`` (config ``humanitarian``), whose
     per-split JSON records are byte-identical in content to the official TSV files;
  2. the official QCRI release archive
     ``crisisnlp.qcri.org/data/crisis_datasets_benchmarks/crisis_datasets_benchmarks_v1.0.tar.gz``
     (``data/all_data_en/crisis_consolidated_humanitarian_filtered_lang_en_*.tsv``).

Raw files are cached under ``REPRO_DATA_CACHE`` and reused on later runs.  A manifest
with source URL, sha256 and row counts is written to ``data/raw/manifest.json``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
import tarfile
import urllib.request
import zipfile  # noqa: F401  (generic archive helper kept for alternative mirrors)

)

COLUMNS = ["id", "event", "source", "text", "lang", "lang_conf", "class_label"]


def _sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def _download(url: str, dest: Path, timeout=120) -> None:
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = dest.with_suffix(dest.suffix + ".part")
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "repro-pipeline/1.0"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp, open(tmp, "wb") as fh:
        while True:
            chunk = resp.read(1 << 20)
            if not chunk:
                break
            fh.write(chunk)
    os.replace(tmp, dest)


def _canonical_path(split: str) -> Path:
    return config.CACHE_DIR / f"{split}.json"


def _load_json_records(path: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        records = json.load(fh)
    df = pd.DataFrame(records)
    return _normalise_columns(df)


def _normalise_columns(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Map column aliases to the release's canonical column names."""
    df = df.copy()
    aliases = {
        "text": ["text", "text_clean", "tweet_text", "tweet"],
        "class_label": ["class_label", "label_humanitarian", "label", "class"],
        "event": ["event", "event_name"],
        "id": ["id", "tweet_id", "tweetid"],
        "source": ["source"],
        "lang": ["lang", "language"],
        "lang_conf": ["lang_conf", "lang conf", "lang_confidence"],
    }
    lower = {c.lower().strip(): c for c in df.columns}
    rename = {}
    for target, names in aliases.items():

            if n in lower:

    df = df.rename(columns=rename)
    for col in COLUMNS:
        if col not in df.columns:

    df = df[COLUMNS].astype(str)

    return df


def _from_official_tarball(dest_dir: Path) -> dict:
    tarball = dest_dir / "crisis_datasets_benchmarks_v1.0.tar.gz"
    if not tarball.exists():
        _download(OFFICIAL_TARBALL, tarball, timeout=600)
    frames = {}
    with tarfile.open(tarball) as tf:
        for split in config.SPLITS:
            member = TSV_TEMPLATE.format(split=split)

    frames = {}

"""Loading, validation and subset construction for the CrisisBench splits.

Implements:
  R1  single-label 11-way multi-class task, 11 labels retained (R14)
  R2  only ``text_clean`` enters the feature matrix; event/source/id/lang/lang_conf are
      never handed to the vectoriser (explicit leakage guard)
  R6  split bookkeeping for the Development-stage protocol
  R7  Train+Development combination for the locked final fit
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from . import acquire, config, preprocess


def load_splits(add_clean_text: bool = True) -> dict:
    frames = acquire.load_frames()
    out = {}
    for split, df in frames.items():
        df = df.reset_index(drop=True)
        if add_clean_text:
            df[config.TEXT_COL] = preprocess.clean_series(df[config.TEXT_RAW_COL])
        out[split] = df
    validate(out)
    return out


def validate(splits: dict) -> dict:
    """Hard structural checks; returns a summary dict."""
    labels = set()
    for split, df in splits.items():
        assert config.TEXT_COL in df.columns, "missing text_clean"
        assert df[config.TEXT_COL].notna().all(), f"{split}: NaN in text_clean"
        empty = int((df[config.TEXT_COL].str.strip() == "").sum())
        assert empty / len(df) < 0.01, f"{split}: {empty} empty cleaned texts"
        assert df[config.LABEL_COL].notna().all(), f"{split}: missing labels"
        labels |= set(df[config.LABEL_COL].str.strip().unique())
        # leakage guard (R2): forbidden columns must never be part of the text feature
        for col in config.EXCLUDED_FEATURE_COLUMNS:
            assert col != config.TEXT_COL
    assert len(labels) == config.N_LABELS_EXPECTED, f"labels: {len(labels)}"
    train_dev = set(splits["train"][config.LABEL_COL]) | set(splits["dev"][config.LABEL_COL])
    unseen = set(splits["test"][config.LABEL_COL]) - train_dev
    assert not unseen, f"Test labels unseen in Train+Dev: {unseen}"
    total = sum(len(df) for df in splits.values())
    summary = {
        "rows": {s: int(len(df)) for s, df in splits.items()},
        "total_rows": int(total),
        "train_plus_dev_rows": int(len(splits["train"]) + len(splits["dev"])),
        "n_labels": len(labels),
        "labels": sorted(labels),
        "label_counts": {s: {k: int(v) for k, v in
                             df[config.LABEL_COL].value_counts().sort_index().items()}
                         for s, df in splits.items()},
    }
    counts = splits["train"][config.LABEL_COL].value_counts()
    summary["imbalance_ratio_train"] = float(counts.max() / counts.min())
    return summary


def labels_order(splits: dict):
    """Fixed label order (sorted union) used for every metric computation (A2)."""
    labels = set()
    for df in splits.values():
        labels |= set(df[config.LABEL_COL].str.strip().unique())
    return np.array(sorted(labels))


def feature_texts(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """The only input handed to the vectoriser (R2)."""
    return df[config.TEXT_COL].astype(str)


def token_stats(series: pd.Series) -> dict:
    lengths = series.str.split().map(len)
    return {
        "mean_tokens": float(lengths.mean()),
        "p95_tokens": float(np.percentile(lengths, 95)),
        "max_tokens": int(lengths.max()),
        "n_rows": int(len(lengths)),
    }


def cyclone_mask(events: pd.Series, strict: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:
    """Case-insensitive event-field match for tropical-cyclone records (A11)."""
    pattern = config.CYCLONE_PATTERN_STRICT if strict else config.CYCLONE_PATTERN_BROAD
    events = events.astype(str)
    return events.str.contains(pattern, case=False, regex=True).fillna(False).values


def smoke_subsample(splits: dict, sizes: dict, seed: int) -> dict:
    """Stratified subsample used by the smoke test."""
    out = {}
    for split, df in splits.items():
        n = min(sizes.get(split, len(df)), len(df))
        parts = []
        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        for label, grp in df.groupby(config.LABEL_COL, sort=True):
            take = max(1, int(round(n * len(grp) / len(df))))
            take = min(take, len(grp))
            idx = rng.permutation(len(grp))[:take]
            parts.append(grp.iloc[idx])
        sub = pd.concat(parts).sample(frac=1.0, random_state=seed).reset_index(drop=True)
        out[split] = sub
    return out

"""The three experimental stages of the paper (R6, R7, R9, R13).

Stage 1  Development checkpoint: vectoriser and classifier fitted on Train only and
         applied unchanged to Development (R6, R9) - the model-selection result.
Stage 2  Locked final model: fresh vectoriser + LinearSVC fitted on Train+Development
         (R7) and evaluated exactly once on the held-out Test split (A10).
Stage 3  Tropical-cyclone comparison (R13): the same locked settings fitted only on
         broad cyclone Train+Development records, and the general model's Test
         predictions filtered to the broad cyclone Test subset.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from . import config, data, modeling


def dev_checkpoint(splits: dict, labels) -> dict:
    tr, dv = splits["train"], splits["dev"]
    y_tr = tr[config.LABEL_COL].values
    y_dv = dv[config.LABEL_COL].values

    t0 = modeling.now()
    vec = modeling.make_vectorizer()
    X_tr = vec.fit_transform(data.feature_texts(tr))
    X_dv = vec.transform(data.feature_texts(dv))
    t_vec = modeling.now() - t0

    t1 = modeling.now()
    clf = modeling.fit_classifier(modeling.make_svc(), X_tr, y_tr)
    t_fit = modeling.now() - t1

    t2 = modeling.now()
    pred = clf.predict(X_dv)
    scores = clf.decision_function(X_dv)
    t_pred = modeling.now() - t2

    res = modeling.evaluate(y_dv, pred, labels, scores=scores)
    res.update({
        "fit_rows": int(X_tr.shape[0]),
        "n_features": int(X_tr.shape[1]),
        "coefficient_shape": list(clf.coef_.shape),
        "max_iter_used": int(clf.max_iter_used),
        "converged": bool(clf.converged),
        "timing_s": {"vectorisation": t_vec, "fitting": t_fit, "prediction": t_pred},
        "dummy_baseline_dev": modeling.dummy_baseline(y_tr, y_dv, labels),
    })
    return res


def final_locked(splits: dict, labels, results_dir) -> dict:
    """Train+Development refit, one Test evaluation (R7, R9, A10)."""
    tr, dv, te = splits["train"], splits["dev"], splits["test"]
    fit_df = pd.concat([tr, dv], ignore_index=True)
    y_fit = fit_df[config.LABEL_COL].values
    y_te = te[config.LABEL_COL].values
    assert len(fit_df) == len(tr) + len(dv)

    t0 = modeling.now()
    vec = modeling.make_vectorizer()
    X_fit = vec.fit_transform(data.feature_texts(fit_df))
    X_te = vec.transform(data.feature_texts(te))
    t_vec = modeling.now() - t0

    t1 = modeling.now()
    clf = modeling.fit_classifier(modeling.make_svc(), X_fit, y_fit)
    t_fit = modeling.now() - t1

    t2 = modeling.now()
    pred = clf.predict(X_te)
    scores = clf.decision_function(X_te)
    t_pred = modeling.now() - t2

    res = modeling.evaluate(y_te, pred, labels, scores=scores)
    res.update({
        "fit_rows": int(X_fit.shape[0]),
        "n_features": int(X_fit.shape[1]),
        "coefficient_shape": list(clf.coef_.shape),
        "train_matrix_mb": float(X_fit.data.nbytes / 1e6),
        "max_iter_used": int(clf.max_iter_used),
        "converged": bool(clf.converged),
        "timing_s": {"vectorisation": t_vec, "fitting": t_fit, "prediction": t_pred},
    })
    pred_path = modeling.save_predictions(
        results_dir / "test_predictions.csv.gz",
        te[config.ID_COL].values, y_te, pred,
        modeling.margins_from_scores(scores), te[config.EVENT_COL].values)
    res["predictions_file"] = pred_path

    # keep the fitted objects for stage 3 and store test predictions
    state = {"vectoriser": vec, "classifier": clf, "y_test": y_te,
             "pred_test": pred, "margin_test": modeling.margins_from_scores(scores),
             "X_test": X_te}
    return {"metrics": res, "state": state}


def cyclone_analysis(splits: dict, labels, state: dict) -> dict:
    """Broad/strict tropical-cyclone specialist vs general comparison (R13, A11)."""
    tr, dv, te = splits["train"], splits["dev"], splits["test"]
    fit_df = pd.concat([tr, dv], ignore_index=True)
    y_fit = fit_df[config.LABEL_COL].values
    y_te = te[config.LABEL_COL].values

    broad_fit = data.cyclone_mask(fit_df[config.EVENT_COL], strict=False)
    strict_fit = data.cyclone_mask(fit_df[config.EVENT_COL], strict=True)
    broad_te = data.cyclone_mask(te[config.EVENT_COL], strict=False)
    strict_te = data.cyclone_mask(te[config.EVENT_COL], strict=True)

    subset_counts = {
        "broad": {"train_plus_dev": int(broad_fit.sum()), "test": int(broad_te.sum()),
                  "total": int(broad_fit.sum() + broad_te.sum())},
        "strict": {"train_plus_dev": int(strict_fit.sum()), "test": int(strict_te.sum()),
                   "total": int(strict_fit.sum() + strict_te.sum())},
        "n_event_strings_broad": int(fit_df.loc[broad_fit, config.EVENT_COL].nunique()

        "broad_event_strings": sorted(set(fit_df.loc[broad_fit, config.EVENT_COL].unique())

    sp_pred = sp_clf.predict(X_sp_te)
    t_pred = modeling.now() - t2

"""Assemble results/metrics.json from the computed stage results.

Every number written here is computed by the pipeline from data; no paper value is
hard-coded or copied into the output.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

from . import config


def _fmt_split(name: str, n: int, role: str) -> str:
    return f"{name} ({n:,} records, {role})"


def build_claims(dev: dict, final: dict, cyclone: dict) -> dict:
    """Map the contract's claims C1-C8 to computed values."""
    claims = {}
    n_test = final["n_records"]
    claims["C1"] = {"metric": "Macro-F1", "value": final["macro_f1"],
                    "split": _fmt_split("Test", n_test, "held out"),
                    "source": "locked LinearSVC (word 1-2gram TF-IDF, C=0.5, balanced) fitted on Train+Development"}
    claims["C2"] = {"metric": "Accuracy", "value": final["accuracy"],
                    "split": _fmt_split("Test", n_test, "held out")}
    claims["C3"] = {"metric": "Weighted-F1", "value": final["weighted_f1"],
                    "split": _fmt_split("Test", n_test, "held out")}
    claims["C4"] = {"metric": "Macro-F1", "value": dev["macro_f1"],
                    "split": _fmt_split("Development", dev["n_records"], "model selection")}
    claims["C5"] = {"metric": "Accuracy", "value": dev["accuracy"],
                    "split": _fmt_split("Development", dev["n_records"], "model selection")}
    if cyclone.get("status") == "ok":
        sp = cyclone["specialist_broad_test"]
        ge = cyclone["general_broad_test"]
        claims["C6"] = {"metric": "Macro-F1", "value": sp["macro_f1"],
                        "split": _fmt_split("Broad tropical-cyclone Test subset", sp["n_records"], "specialist model")}
        claims["C7"] = {"metric": "Macro-F1", "value": ge["macro_f1"],
                        "split": _fmt_split("Broad tropical-cyclone Test subset", ge["n_records"], "general locked model")}
    else:
        claims["C6"] = {"metric": "Macro-F1", "value": None, "status": cyclone.get("status")}
        claims["C7"] = {"metric": "Macro-F1", "value": None, "status": cyclone.get("status")}
    claims["C8"] = {"metric": "TF-IDF feature count", "value": final["n_features"],
                    "split": _fmt_split("Train+Development fitting data", final["fit_rows"], "vectoriser fit")}
    return claims


def build_report(dev: dict, final: dict, cyclone: dict, split_summary: dict,
                 manifest: dict, runtime_s: float, mode: str = "full",
                 dataset_rowcounts: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    claims = build_claims(dev, final, cyclone)
    config_echo = {
        "text_input": "text_clean only (event/source/id/lang/lang_conf excluded)",
        "preprocessing": ["html_unescape", "strip leading RT", "URL->url", "@mention->user",
                          "delete '#' keep hashtag text", "whitespace collapse", "lowercase"],
        "no_stopwords_stemming_lemmatisation": True,
        "tfidf": {k: (list(v) if isinstance(v, tuple) else v) for k, v in config.TFIDF_PARAMS.items()},
        "classifier": {"estimator": "sklearn.svm.LinearSVC", **{
            k: v for k, v in config.SVC_PARAMS.items()}},
        "dev_stage_fit": "vectoriser + classifier fitted on Train only, applied to Development",
        "final_fit": "fresh vectoriser + classifier fitted on Train+Development, one Test evaluation",
        "cyclone_specialist": "same locked settings, fitted on broad cyclone Train+Development records",
        "cyclone_filters": {"strict": config.CYCLONE_PATTERN_STRICT,
                            "broad": config.CYCLONE_PATTERN_BROAD},
        "metrics": "Accuracy, Macro-F1, Weighted-F1 over the 11 fixed labels, zero_division=0",
        "decision_margin": "highest minus second-highest decision score",
    }
    notes = (
        "Reimplementation from the paper (no author code). CrisisBench v1.0 English "
        "humanitarian files were obtained from the official QCRI release / its Hugging Face "
        "mirror; the obtained release is very slightly larger per split than the row counts "
        "stated in the paper (<0.25% per split, <0.15% overall), so differences of that order "
        "in the evaluated numbers can come from the data snapshot rather than the pipeline. "
        "The locked Test model is fitted once on Train+Development and evaluated once on Test; "
        "no test-based tuning is performed. Development-stage numbers come from a vectoriser "
        "fitted on Train only."
    )
    if mode == "smoke":
        notes += " SMOKE MODE: metrics come from a stratified subsample, not the full splits."
    report = {
        "metric": "Macro-F1",
        "value": claims["C1"]["value"],
        "dataset": config.DATASET_NAME,
        "split": claims["C1"]["split"],
        "mode": mode,
        "config": config_echo,
        "notes": notes,
        "claims": claims,
        "dataset_manifest": {
            "source_url": manifest["source_url"],
            "files": manifest["files"],
            "rows": split_summary["rows"],
            "total_rows": split_summary["total_rows"],
            "train_plus_dev_rows": split_summary["train_plus_dev_rows"],
            "n_labels": split_summary["n_labels"],
            "labels": split_summary["labels"],
            "label_counts": split_summary["label_counts"],
            "imbalance_ratio_train": split_summary["imbalance_ratio_train"],
        },
        "stages": {
            "dev_checkpoint": dev,
            "locked_final_test": final,
            "cyclone": cyclone,
        },
        "runtime_seconds": runtime_s,
    }
    if dataset_rowcounts:
        report["dataset_manifest"]["token_stats_train"] = dataset_rowcounts
    return report


def write(report: dict, path) -> str:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(report, fh, indent=2)
    return str(path)

"""Reproduce the paper's locked CrisisBench LinearSVC results from scratch.

Usage
-----
    python reproduce.py            # full run -> results/metrics.json
    python reproduce.py --smoke    # stratified subsample -> results/smoke_metrics.json
    python reproduce.py --force-download

Stages: acquire/validate data -> Development checkpoint (Train-only fit) -> locked
Train+Development refit with one held-out Test evaluation -> tropical-cyclone
specialist vs general comparison -> results/metrics.json.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
import time
import traceback

if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

from src import acquire, config, data, experiments, modeling, preprocess, report


def run(mode: str = "full", force_download: bool = False) -> dict:
    t_start = time.perf_counter()
    config.RESULTS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    config.LOGS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    print("[1/5] acquiring CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian files ...")
    manifest = acquire.acquire(force=force_download)

    print("[2/5] loading + validating splits, building text_clean ...")
    splits = data.load_splits()
    split_summary = data.validate(splits)
    print("      rows:", split_summary["rows"],
          "train+dev:", split_summary["train_plus_dev_rows"],
          "labels:", split_summary["n_labels"])
    tok = data.token_stats(splits["train"][config.TEXT_COL])
    print(f"      tokens: mean={tok['mean_tokens']:.1f} p95={tok['p95_tokens']:.0f}")
    examples = preprocess.audit_examples(splits["train"][config.TEXT_RAW_COL], 20)
    with open(config.LOGS_DIR / "preprocess_examples.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        import json
        json.dump({"token_stats": tok, "examples": examples}, fh, indent=2)

    labels = data.labels_order(splits)

    if mode == "smoke":
        print("[2b/5] smoke mode: stratified subsample")
        splits = data.smoke_subsample(splits, config.SMOKE_SIZES, config.SMOKE_SEED)
        split_summary = data.validate(splits)
        labels = data.labels_order(splits)
        print("      subsample rows:", split_summary["rows"])

    print("[3/5] Development-stage checkpoint (vectoriser+classifier fitted on Train only) ...")
    dev = experiments.dev_checkpoint(splits, labels)
    print(f"      Dev  Accuracy={dev['accuracy']:.4f}  Macro-F1={dev['macro_f1']:.4f}  "
          f"Weighted-F1={dev['weighted_f1']:.4f}  features={dev['n_features']}  "
          f"(max_iter={dev['max_iter_used']}, converged={dev['converged']})")
    print(f"      dummy baseline on Dev: Acc={dev['dummy_baseline_dev']['accuracy']:.4f} "
          f"Macro-F1={dev['dummy_baseline_dev']['macro_f1']:.4f}")

    print("[4/5] locked final model: Train+Development refit, single Test evaluation ...")
    final_out = experiments.final_locked(splits, labels, config.RESULTS_DIR)
    final = final_out["metrics"]
    print(f"      Test Accuracy={final['accuracy']:.4f}  Macro-F1={final['macro_f1']:.4f}  "
          f"Weighted-F1={final['weighted_f1']:.4f}  features={final['n_features']}  "
          f"fit rows={final['fit_rows']}")

    print("[5/5] tropical-cyclone specialist vs general locked model ...")
    cyclone = experiments.cyclone_analysis(splits, labels, final_out["state"])
    if cyclone.get("status") == "ok":
        sp, ge = cyclone["specialist_broad_test"], cyclone["general_broad_test"]
        print(f"      broad Test subset n={sp['n_records']}: specialist Macro-F1={sp['macro_f1']:.4f} "
              f"(features={sp['n_features']}), general Macro-F1={ge['macro_f1']:.4f}")
        print(f"      broad subset sizes: {cyclone['subsets']['broad']}")
    else:
        print("      ", cyclone.get("status"))

    runtime = time.perf_counter() - t_start
    rep = report.build_report(dev, final, cyclone, split_summary, manifest, runtime,
                              mode=mode, dataset_rowcounts=tok)
    out = config.RESULTS_DIR / ("metrics.json" if mode == "full" else "smoke_metrics.json")
    path = report.write(rep, out)
    print(f"\nwrote {path}  (runtime {runtime:.1f} s)")
    print(f"TARGET: Test Macro-F1 = {final['macro_f1']:.4f} | Accuracy = "
          f"{final['accuracy']:.4f} | Weighted-F1 = {final['weighted_f1']:.4f}")
    return rep


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="stratified subsample end-to-end test")
    ap.add_argument("--force-download", action="store_true", help="ignore cached raw files")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    mode = "smoke" if args.smoke else "full"
    try:
        run(mode=mode, force_download=args.force_download)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        traceback.print_exc()
        print("REPRODUCTION FAILED", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Smoke test: end-to-end pipeline on a stratified 3,000/1,000/1,000 subsample.

Asserts that the JSON report parses, that claims C1-C8, per-label metrics, margins and
timings are present, that all metrics are finite and in [0, 1], and that the coefficient
matrix has shape (n_labels, n_features).

Run with:  python tests/smoke_test.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

import reproduce  # noqa: E402
from src import config  # noqa: E402


def main() -> int:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rep = reproduce.run(mode="smoke")
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0

    path = config.RESULTS_DIR / "smoke_metrics.json"
    obj = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    for key in ("metric", "value", "dataset", "split", "config", "notes", "claims", "stages"):
        assert key in obj, f"missing key {key}"
    for cid in [f"C{i}" for i in range(1, 9)]:
        assert cid in obj["claims"], f"missing claim {cid}"

    dev = obj["stages"]["dev_checkpoint"]
    fin = obj["stages"]["locked_final_test"]
    for stage_name, stage in (("dev", dev), ("test", fin)):
        for m in ("accuracy", "macro_f1", "weighted_f1"):
            v = stage[m]
            assert isinstance(v, float) and math.isfinite(v) and 0.0 <= v <= 1.0, (stage_name, m, v)
        assert stage["coefficient_shape"][0] == 11
        assert stage["coefficient_shape"][1] == stage["n_features"]
        assert len(stage["per_label"]) == 11
        assert math.isfinite(stage["margin"]["mean"]) and stage["margin"]["mean"] >= 0
        for k in ("vectorisation", "fitting", "prediction"):
            assert stage["timing_s"][k] >= 0

    cyc = obj["stages"]["cyclone"]
    assert "subsets" in cyc
    if cyc.get("status") == "ok":
        for m in ("macro_f1", "accuracy"):
            assert 0.0 <= cyc["specialist_broad_test"][m] <= 1.0

    assert obj["mode"] == "smoke"
    print(f"\nSMOKE TEST OK in {elapsed:.1f}s  (report: {path})")
    assert elapsed < 600, "smoke run should stay well below the full-run budget"
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

audit_summary: The implementation faithfully follows the paper's locked method: word unigram-bigram TF-IDF with min_df=2, max_df=0.95, sublinear L2-normalised float32 features, and LinearSVC with C=0.5 and balanced class weighting, refit on Train+Development and evaluated once on Test. All 14 requirements are met or, for R1's row count, only partially met because the official release obtained has 87,557 rows rather than the paper's 87,455 (0.12% higher); the HF mirror was verified byte-for-byte identical to the official QCRI TSV, so this is a release-snapshot difference, not a dataset substitution. Every reported number is computed from the loaded data: paper_numbers_found_in_code is empty, config.py stores no result values, and report.py maps stage metrics directly. The headline values match closely (Test Macro-F1 0.6584 vs 0.6578, Accuracy 0.8284 vs 0.8282, Weighted-F1 0.8317 vs 0.8315; Dev 0.6432/0.8249 vs 0.6413/0.8245; cyclone specialist 0.5477 vs 0.5455 and general 0.5302 vs 0.5276), with differences consistent with the 0.12% larger data snapshot. C8 is close but not within an absolute 0.01 band (110,330 vs 110,414 features); the implementer's 'largest gap 0.0006' summary applies only to the fractional metrics, not to the feature count. Minor reporting differences remain: Table 7's 11.62 MB sparse-matrix size corresponds to the full CSR structure whereas the code reports data.nbytes (5.95 MB), and timings are slower than the paper (7.6s/18.2s vs 2.2s/1.9s), likely due to environment or sklearn version; neither affects the result claims. No hardcoding, echoed paper numbers, proxy metrics, wrong splits or scale-down was found.

requirement_check.evidence: 11 labels and single-label multi-class confirmed; obtained 87,557 rows (61,235/8,957/17,365) from the official QCRI release via the HF mirror, while the paper states 87,455. The HF mirror was verified identical to the official CrisisBench TSV files (text, label and event columns), so the 102-row difference is a release-snapshot discrepancy, not a different dataset.

Only text_clean feeds the vectoriser via data.feature_texts(); config excludes event/source/id/lang/lang_conf, and data.validate() asserts the leakage guard. The vectoriser is never given the excluded columns.

preprocess.clean_text performs html.unescape, leading-RT removal, URL->'url', @mention->'user', '#' deletion while retaining hashtag text, whitespace collapse and lowercase; logs/preprocess_examples.json shows before/after examples conforming to R3.
TFIDF_PARAMS sets stop_words=None and uses the default sklearn token_pattern; no stemming, lemmatisation or separate custom tokenisation is applied.
TfidfVectorizer(analyzer='word', ngram_range=(1,2), min_df=2, max_df=0.95, sublinear_tf=True, norm='l2', dtype=np.float32) exactly as specified.
experiments.dev_checkpoint fits the vectoriser on Train only (61,235 rows) and transforms Development (8,957 rows); Test is not used in this stage.

experiments.final_locked concatenates Train+Development and refits a fresh vectoriser and LinearSVC (70,192 fitting rows vs the paper's 70,099, a difference inherited from the 0.12% larger release snapshot).
modeling.make_svc uses LinearSVC(C=0.5, class_weight='balanced', penalty='l2', loss='squared_hinge') with word unigram-bigram TF-IDF, matching the locked configuration.

Development-stage selection uses Train-only fit and Dev evaluation; the locked Test split is evaluated exactly once in final_locked. Although an early scratch script printed Test metrics during exploration, the final reproduce.py has no test-based branching or tuning.
The pipeline uses sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer and sklearn.svm.LinearSVC throughout.
modeling.evaluate returns accuracy, macro_f1, weighted_f1, per-label precision/recall/F1/support and the confusion matrix over all 11 labels.
modeling.margins_from_scores computes np.partition(scores, -2) and subtracts the second-highest from the highest decision score; the margin summaries are written to results/metrics.json.

experiments.cyclone_analysis fits the specialist with the same locked TF-IDF/LinearSVC settings on broad cyclone Train+Development records (17,612) and evaluates on the broad cyclone Test subset (4,361), with case-insensitive event matching (typhoon|hurricane|cyclone).
All 11 CrisisBench labels are retained; labels_order returns the sorted union of all labels and every metric call passes labels=all 11, with no merging.
